newsitem.title: CHINA: Corrosion seen costing China $24.1 bln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Corrosion seen costing China $24.1 bln in 1996.

text.p: China plans to cut down on industrial corrosion, which is expected to cost the country an estimated 200 billion yuan ($24.1 billion) in 1996, the China Daily said on Friday.

The Ministry of Chemical Industry had drafted a plan to reduce losses caused by corrosion by 60-80 billion yuan ($7.2-9.6 billion) annually over the next five years, it said, quoting ministry official Fan Yong.
The ministry planned to introduce advanced anti-corrosion technology and equipment from abroad, it said.

Losses caused by corrosion were six times those caused by natural disasters and would cost China an estimated 300 billion yuan ($36.14 billion) annually by 2000 if anti-corrosion measures were not taken, the newspaper said. It gave no further details.
